<description>
Part of https://github.com/bitcoin-core/gui-qml/issues/1008.

The QML GUI shows "Transaction sent" even when the node rejected the transaction, because `CWallet::CommitTransaction()` only logs the rejection and returns `void`.
This PR bubbles up the submission result through `interfaces::Wallet::commitTransaction()` so the GUI can report it.

#### Key changes
- Introduce `TransactionBroadcastError`, holding a `TransactionError` code and an untranslated message.
- Commit/Broadcast functions returns `Expected<void, TransactionBroadcastError>`.
  - Remove `TransactionError::OK`, a success value in an error enum.
- Add a `SUBMISSION_SKIPPED` code for when the wallet doesn't submit the transaction (broadcasting disabled, abandoned, coinbase, confirmed or conflicted). `SubmitTxMemoryPoolAndRelay()` previously returned `false` in these cases.

#### Note
- Existing callers (wallet RPCs, Qt widgets, fee bumper) ignore the new result, so their behavior and RPC responses don't change.
- `commitBumpTransaction()` similarly reports success for a rejected replacement. This will be addressed in a follow-up PR.
- gui-qml will need to update its `interfaces::Wallet` mock for the new `commitTransaction()` signature.
</description>

<commits>
9f1fbcddb3 refactor: use Expected for transaction broadcast results

Introduce TransactionBroadcastError, which holds a TransactionError and
a message. BroadcastTransaction returns
Expected<void, TransactionBroadcastError>, so the error code and its message
travel together. Remove TransactionError::OK.

Errors that had an empty message now carry the generic
TransactionErrorString text.

9f46840bac wallet: report skipped transaction submissions

Return Expected<void, TransactionBroadcastError> from
SubmitTxMemoryPoolAndRelay. Wallet-side prechecks (broadcasting
disabled, coinbase, abandoned, confirmed or conflicted) return the new
SUBMISSION_SKIPPED code with a reason; node errors pass through.

744650bc9a wallet: propagate submission errors through commit APIs

Return the submission result from CWallet::CommitTransaction and
interfaces::Wallet::commitTransaction, so callers can tell whether a
saved transaction was accepted.

4e3d167559 test: cover CommitTransaction results

Check the CommitTransaction result for accepted, already confirmed,
max-fee and mempool-minimum rejections, and that a rejected transaction
stays saved in the wallet.

Also check the result through interfaces::Wallet::commitTransaction,
which the GUI uses, for skipped and accepted commits.
</commits>
